habitat: Singly or in pairs on shallow ponds with surface and fringing vegetation, vleis and flooded grassland. It arrives in large numbers in temporarily suitable habitat.
summary: An uncommon summer resident. Smaller and more secretive than Common Moorhen, with paler grey or greenish plumage. The bill is mostly yellow, with red only on the culmen and a pointed frontal shield. The legs are greenish or red-brown and lack the red tibial rings. The immature is much duller. The call is three to five rapid hoots, tu-tu-tu. Newman does not name the months, so they are unset. The Kemp name Lesser Moorhen and the code VB were left unchanged.

similar.note: Common Moorhen is larger, with a red bill, a rounded shield and a red band on the tibia.

The back colour is only described as paler grey or greenish.
A flight pattern was not described.

calls.description: Three to five rapid hoots, tu-tu-tu. Grade A call and flight call from Marracuene, Maputo, Mozambique, with another species in the background. The filename is XC407075-DR0000_0169.mp3.
